title: The photo accepts any file type and any size
hint: The rules promise a type and a size limit. Does anything enforce them besides the file picker? A big photo or a dropped file will tell.
explanation: accept="image/*" is only a suggestion for the file picker. Drag and drop bypasses it, and there is no check of the MIME type or of the 2 MB limit in the code.

title: A non-square photo is stretched in the preview
hint: Not every photo is a square. Try a landscape one.
explanation: The preview has a fixed width and height but no object-fit: cover, so the image is squeezed to fit the circle.

title: The 10 MB limit is not enforced
hint: The rules promise a size limit. Find a file that breaks it.
explanation: The limit is converted to bytes with one extra * 1024, so it is really 10 GB. A large file passes without an error.

title: Files with an upper-case extension are rejected: REPORT.PDF
hint: Scanners and old cameras love shouting in file names.
explanation: The extension is compared with endsWith('.pdf') without lowercasing the name, so .PDF, .JPG and .Png are reported as unsupported.

title: The file name is rendered as HTML (XSS)
hint: A file name is user input too. What if it contains markup?
explanation: The name is inserted with dangerouslySetInnerHTML, so renaming a file to runs a script. The same works with a real file name on macOS or Linux.

title: File sizes use the wrong unit: a 3 MB file shows as 3.0 KB
hint: Compare the size in the list with what your file manager says.
explanation: The size is divided by 1024 twice (megabytes) but labelled "KB".

title: Upload progress ends at 105%
hint: Watch the percentage closely until the upload finishes.
explanation: Progress grows in steps of 7 and is never clamped to 100, so the last step overshoots.

title: The progress bar is invisible to assistive technologies
hint: How does a screen reader know how far the upload is?
explanation: The bar is a plain div without role="progressbar" and aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax.

title: Removing one file removes every file with the same name
hint: Upload the same file twice, then remove only one of the copies.
explanation: Files are removed by name instead of by id, so all duplicates disappear together.

title: The 5 file limit can be exceeded by adding files in several batches
hint: The limit works for one selection. What about the second one?
explanation: Only the new selection is compared with the limit, files already in the list are not counted. 3 + 3 files are accepted.

title: Documents cannot be added with the keyboard
hint: Put the mouse away and try to upload a document.
explanation: The drop zone is a div with onClick, without role="button" or tabindex, and the file input has display: none, so neither of them can be focused.

title: Save works while uploads are still in progress
hint: Do not wait for the uploads to finish.
explanation: The button is never disabled and the handler does not check progress, so unfinished files are reported as saved.

title: The counter says 10 files, the rules say 5
hint: Two places on the page talk about the same limit.
explanation: The counter is hardcoded as "/ 10 files" while the rules and the code limit the list to 5.

title: A PNG photo throws an uncaught error in the console
hint: Pick a PNG or a screenshot as the photo and check the Console.
explanation: EXIF data exists only in JPEG photos. For any other file readExif returns null, the code reads null.orientation and the promise rejects with "Uncaught (in promise) TypeError". The orientation is never applied.

title: On a phone in landscape the drop zone collapses
hint: Turn the phone sideways, or make the window very short.
explanation: For screens lower than 500px in landscape the drop zone gets a fixed height of 40px with overflow: hidden. Its text is cut and the area is hard to hit. Fixed heights break as soon as the content does not fit.
